subject: Clarifying erase windows, backups, and our 'no-train' boundary
messages:
From: Alice Brown <alice.brown@finpulse.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finpulse.com
Date: 2026-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on data handling: do you ever train on customer data?

Hi Neha,

Quick one from our security & privacy review: FinPulse is evaluating Redwood for transaction-processing prompts. We need clarity on two related items before we finish our internal risk assessment: 

1) Your public language says you "do not train on customer data" — can you confirm whether that applies to all deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private)? Are there any edge cases where data may be used to improve models (even aggregated/derivative)?

2) Retention and backups: what are the retention tiers (live, tombstoned, backups/snapshots), who controls TTLs, and do backups/snapshots ever flow into any analytics or model-training pipelines? If you could call out the SLA for deletion requests (e.g., erase window) that would be helpful.

I attached our security questionnaire (pdf). If easier, we can do a 30-min call. Thanks — Alice

--
Alice Brown
Security Review Lead | FinPulse Corp

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on data handling: do you ever train on customer data?

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the clear questions — happy to clarify. Short answer up front: Redwood provides a formal non-training commitment for customer data used with (a) Dedicated and (b) Private deployments, and for Hosted API we offer a configurable "no-training" tenancy/option for customers who require it. In all modes, we do not include customer-provided production text in our training corpus by default.

High-level bullets:
- Scope of "no-train": customer request can be applied at account or project level. When applied, we exclude customer traffic from all model training and large-scale fine-tuning pipelines (no derivatives).
- Backups & snapshots: backups are separated by storage tier (hot logs, warm backups, archival snapshots). Backups and snapshots are treated as operational artifacts — they are not routed into ML training pipelines.
- Tombstones & TTLs: customers can set a retention TTL for application-level data where applicable; tombstoned records are marked and purged per configured window.
- Forensics & debug: ephemeral debug snapshots used for short-term troubleshooting are retained only for a short TTL and are scoped to support tickets. They are isolated and tagged to prevent inclusion in downstream analytics.

I attached a short attestation (nontraining-attestation.pdf) and a CSV summary of retention tiers you can use in your questionnaire. If it helps, I can add a paragraph about KMS separation and SAS roles for Dedicated/Private.

Would you like a live call — I can loop in Marissa from Legal if you want an audit/attestation review in the same session.

Best,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Alice — great questions. Below is a concise Q&A we typically provide for security reviews. I've also linked our internal runbook (read-only link) and the HubSpot ticket for traceability.

1) Residency for backups/snapshots:
- Primary storage and customer-configured Dedicated/Private deployments remain in the region you select.
- Operational backups follow the same region-first policy; cross-region replication only occurs when explicitly enabled for DR (disaster recovery) and is documented in the service configuration. For Hosted accounts, we can restrict backups to a given region during onboarding.

2) Debug snapshots & PII escalation:
- Debug snapshots are retained for up to 14 days by default (shorter per request); they are flagged with a support-ticket ID and access is scoped to SRE/support engineers with justification logged.
- If PII is found in a snapshot we trigger the incident workflow: snapshot isolation, expedited purge (within 48 hours), and a forensic export of the access log for the customer. We can also route the snapshot through a secure deletion flow if requested.

3) Audit evidence that backups were not used for training:
- We provide a signed non-training attestation (attached).
- Audit logs: requestable logs show ingestion and dataset flows; these logs include checksums and object identifiers for snapshots and backups so you can verify provenance.
- Model training pipelines are logically separated; we maintain records showing dataset manifests used for training jobs and can produce redacted manifests for audits.

4) Deletion/erase SLA (examples):
- Application-level ephemeral messages: 0–2 business days to mark tombstoned, 3–10 business days to purge from active indexes (depends on shard cycles).
- Warm backups: typically 7–30 business days to permanently remove an object (subject to DR replication topology).
- Long-term archival: retention-bound deletion follows the configured retention TTL and may require separate archival purge workflows (we'll provide an exact timeline during contracting).

5) Extra controls for FinPulse:
- For Dedicated/Private we can enforce customer-managed KMS so Redwood cannot access plain-text content for any backups or snapshots.
- Optionally, we can provide per-tenant logging exports and a signed attestation on request that training pipelines did not consume specified object IDs.

Next steps: I will start a formal attestation workflow with Legal. Marissa, Ben — can you review the attestation draft and the proposed audit artifacts below? If you prefer I can open an NDA/Statement of Work addendum for backup residency.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/FP-4021
Docs: https://docs.redwood.com/security/data-retention#no-train-pledge

Best,
Neha

Attachments referenced: nontraining-attestation.pdf
